atoms.a: Jacob has gone to a farmers’ market to buy some fruit and veg. If each pepper costs 23p, which expression can be used to work out the cost, <u>in pence</u>, for any amount of peppers, n?
How much will it cost for Jacob to buy four peppers?
Next, Jacob goes to buy some cauliflowers. If each cauliflower costs £1.50, which expression can be used to work out the cost, <u>in pounds</u>, for any amount of cauliflowers, n?
How much will it cost, <u>in pounds</u>, for Jacob to buy three cauliflowers?
Finally, Jacob buys some potatoes. If potatoes cost £1.52 per kilogram, which expression can be used to work out the cost, <u>in pence</u>, for any weight of potatoes, n, in kilograms?

feedback.wrong: Careful, the answer needs to have the cost in pence. What is £1.52 in pence?

atoms.a: How much will it cost, <u>in pence</u>, for Jacob to buy 500g of potatoes?
atoms.sound: How much will it cost, <u>in pence</u>, for Jacob to buy 500 grams of potatoes?

wrong.text: 500 g is equivalent to 0.5 kg. Multiplying a number by 0.5 is the same as dividing by 2.
